why: displayWidth in localizeExamples.ts is measured a second time in Python, by display_width in backend/tests/test_example_descriptions.py, so that one description cap can be checked on both sides. Two implementations of one measurement drift silently, so both read these vectors and assert against them. One table, two readers: change a width here and both tests have to be right about it.
coverage: The prose vectors below are what descriptions actually contain; the single characters after them are one per wide range, so that dropping or mistyping any one range in either port fails here rather than shipping. A range's own bounds are pinned only where a real assigned character sits on both sides of them (U+303E/U+303F, U+FF60/U+FF61, and the four narrow neighbours just past a range's top) -- most of these ranges end on an unassigned code point, which is not something to pin a test to. U+F900 is written as an escape on purpose: it is a compatibility ideograph that looks exactly like U+8C48 and normalises to it, so a literal character here would silently move to another range.
